To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we have parametrized a molecular model of SDS within the Gromacs software package, (2) we have used this model to investigate the kinetics of SDS aggregation, (3) we have identified a structural transition in the SDS aggregates brought upon by temperature, and (4) we have shown that this transition is associated with a change in aggregation kinetics.
we have developed a molecular dynamics model for sodium dodecysulfate (SDS), which we used to study its aggregation behavior in solution.
we have developed a molecular model of SDS, and we have used it to simulate the aggregation process of SDS in aqueous solution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural and dynamical properties of ionic surfactant aggregates.
the structural properties of SDS aggregates and their dependence on temperature and surfactant concentration.
the structural properties of surfactant aggregates in aqueous solution, and the results are expected to contribute to a better understanding of the behavior of surfactants in solution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

SDS micelles are formed through a two-step process, which involves a nucleation step, followed by a subsequent growth of the aggregate, which occurs through the attachment of new molecules to the surface of the aggregate, and the rearrangement of existing ones.

the structural transition is a consequence of a competition between the hydrophobic effect, which favors the formation of a crystalline aggregate, and the electrostatic interactions, which favor the formation of micelles.
the surfactant aggregation process is a function of temperature, concentration, ionic strength, and pH. The present work provides the first molecular level description of this process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the structural properties of the surfactant aggregate are highly dependent on temperature.
the transition is driven by a competition between the enthalpy of the hydrophilic headgroups and the entropy of the hydrophobic tails.
we have been able to capture the transition from micelle to crystal in SDS aggregates through molecular dynamics simulations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the surfactant aggregation is a complex phenomenon involving a number of structural changes.

the surfactant molecules in the micelles are more flexible than those in the crystalline aggregates, which is reflected in a higher number of hydrogen bonds and in a larger number of water molecules that penetrate the micellar structure.
the structural properties of the surfactant aggregate can be controlled by the temperature and surfactant concentration.
